The FOMC statement points to a solid macro backdrop—strong job gains, low unemployment, inflation near 2 percent, and an accommodative policy stance with balanced risks and a path of gradual hikes. Incorporating the contemporaneous SLOOS, bank lending conditions do not appear to be a headwind: standards and terms for C&I loans to large and middle‑market firms were generally unchanged to modestly easier amid competition, while CRE standards remained somewhat tighter and consumer credit was mixed (e.g., some tightening in autos). On net, SLOOS suggests credit supply is broadly supportive of growth, modestly reinforcing the positive tone of the statement. Accordingly, I tilt the assessment slightly more positive than the baseline.
